newsitem.title: USA: Sultan's alleged 'sex toy' sues for $90 million.
newsitem.headline: Sultan's alleged 'sex toy' sues for $90 million.

text.p: A former Miss USA beauty queen who alleges the Sultan of Brunei tried to turn her into his "sexual toy" is suing the world's richest man and others for more than $90 million, according to court papers.
In her federal lawsuit, Shannon Marketic says she was duped into believing she was going to Brunei for modeling and promotional work, while the real purpose was "to use her only as a sexual toy."
Marketic, 26, filed her suit in U.S. District Court in Los Angeles in January, when it was sealed. A judge on Wednesday unsealed the papers in the case.

Earlier this month, the sultan "categorically" denied the allegations in a statement from the Brunei prime minister's office. "His Majesty, the sultan ... has never been acquainted with, nor met, Ms. Marketic," the statement said.

The lawsuit says Marketic was among seven attractive young women sent to Brunei -- an oil-rich sultanate on the island of Borneo in the South China Sea -- by a Los Angeles talent agency. When they arrived, their passports and return tickets were taken from them and they were transported to the sultan's palace, which included seven mansions and a sports complex, the lawsuit states.
The suit names the sultan, Haji Hassanal Bolkiah, and his brother, Prince Jaji Jefri Bolkiah, as co-defendants. The sultan is generally believed to be the richest person in the world.

Marketic, who was Miss California in 1992 and Miss USA from 1992 to 1993, sued in U.S. federal court because both the sultan and the prince, through companies they own, do business in the United States, the suit says.

She alleged the women were taken inside the sports complex, where there were several hard-core pornography magazines lying on tables. They were ordered to dance at late night "parties" seven times a week, when the sultan and his guests would grope at them while shouting lewd comments, the lawsuit says.
Marketic said one of the sultan's guests shouted at her, "What do you think you are here for? You might have been Miss USA but you're a whore now."

Her lawsuit also says one of the sultan's guests kept repeating at the parties that Marketic was not wearing panties, "and at times he would grab her private parts in unsuccessfully attempting to prove his point."

"On other occasions at these parties, plaintiff's dress would be pulled up for the reason of seeing what color her panties were," the lawsuit contends. It also alleges that if the women were told they were going to "tea" or not to wear makeup, that meant they were going to have sex with the man with whom they were having "tea."
Marketic said that after the first day in Brunei, when she realized sex was expected of her and the other women, she asked to go home but was told she had to stay.

When they were not at the "parties" or having "tea" the women were "basically under house arrest" and were forced to watch movies, "much of which ... dealt with women, particularly models, being abused and/or killed," the lawsuit states.

Marketic said that after 32 days of being "forcibly detained" in Brunei she was given her passport and return ticket and told she had 20 minutes to pack. She was also given $10,000 -- much less than than the $21,000 a week promised in her contract.

She is also suing Los Angeles-based Kaliber Talent Consultants, Inc. and the Kaliber Talent Consulting Corp., as well as Elizabeth Khan and her brother David Khan, who operate the two agencies. The beauty queen said the Khans told her her job in Brunei would be modeling and promotion and that there would be no sex involved while knowing full well that the real purpose was to use her as a "prostitute."
The Khans and their lawyer were not immediately available for comment. No date has been set for a hearing in the case.
